column1: 1. Before the study: fill Information & Goals, then list everything the team expects to see on the Observations & Assumptions tab. Start each of those rows with * so it's marked as an assumption.
2. Fill Participants as sessions are scheduled. Mark high-value participants with *.
3. List the tasks on Tasks & Metrics before the first session, but leave the scores blank until the study runs.
4. During or right after each session: put a 1 in that participant's column for every observation you saw. Add a new row for anything new, even if only one person did it.
5. Use Notes for anything that doesn't fit another tab: context, tools they use, quotes that explain an outlier.
6. After the study: fill the task scores, then summarize on General & Post Interview.
One observation per row, written as what the participant did or said, not your interpretation.
Give each participant column its own fill color so patterns show across a row at a glance. That's the rainbow.
Never delete a row because only one person did it. Count sorts rows; it doesn't decide what matters.
Assumption rows (*) get marked like any other row. A * row with few marks is a refuted assumption, which is a finding.
Possible solution is optional and separate from the observation. Notes hold the why: what the participant said, their setup, their workaround.
Use participant IDs (P1, P2) here. Keep names and contact details on the Participants tab only, and remove them before sharing the sheet.
